ctx.x: Do you remember what you played for the Mother's Day crowd?

I played Schubert's 'Serenade' -- I think that was the name of it. The thing that had the least notes in it. 'Cause I never saw 6,000 people in front of me, a hundred and some people behind me in the choir, a hundred and some people sitting on the side of me in the orchestra, and that infernal red light on that broadcasting machine. That was a little too much.
A funny thing. In all my musical career, I never forgot that -- that feeling of complete mystification of all of this thing going on at once. And until today I'm terrifically stage frighted --
